title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. played 2B with a lollipop in his mouth. Aaron Boone was not happy
content:
New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. won’t play baseball with a cup, but he will take the field with a green lollipop in his mouth.

Chisholm caused a stir Monday night after YES Network’s cameras caught the 28-year-old sucking on a lollipop with the Yankees trailing 4-1 against the Detroit Tigers. Yankees manager Aaron Boone did not know his second baseman had taken the field with candy in his mouth until he was made aware of it postgame Monday. He was not pleased by the optics.

“I just don’t think he should have had a lollipop out on the field,” Boone told reporters, via the YES Network. “It wasn’t a good look to me. That’s that.”

Boone said he spoke with Chisholm about the incident and expects that it won’t happen again. It wasn’t the first time this season Chisholm played with a lollipop in his mouth. Against the Boston Red Sox in April, Chisholm took an at-bat with a lollipop, which Boone was also unaware of.

Boone said he was “annoyed” with Chisholm’s choice but added that “it’s not that big a deal.” Chisholm is in the lineup for Tuesday’s game against the Tigers.

“It just bothered me,” Boone said. “It was addressed. I don’t think there’s any ill will. I just don’t think that should be part of what we’re doing.”

This is the latest in what has already been an eventful year for the pending free agent. In spring training, Chisholm said he expected that he would become the second member of the 50-50 club. He also said he was looking for a contract worth over $300 million. He got off to a painfully slow start at the plate, not hitting his first home run until April 23. Since then, Chisholm has been one of New York’s best players, posting a 125 wRC+, the fifth-best mark among regular Yankees.

“I think he’s definitely stabilized the last month-plus,” Boone said. “I expect a lot from him. I expect more. He should be one of the game’s better players. I still feel like he still has that hot streak in him to where he plays super well. He’s capable of that, and that’s my expectation for him.”

Last week, Chisholm left a game in the middle of an at-bat after fouling a ball off his groin. He was ultimately OK after the pain subsided, but it still did not cause him to change his mind about wearing proper protection.

After a private conversation with his manager, he won’t have a lollipop as an accessory on the field, either.
